parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the resistivity $\rho$ of the material of the resistance wire.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The switch is open.
State the reading on the voltmeter.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The switch is now closed.
State whether there is an increase, decrease or no change to:
- the current in the battery
- the voltmeter reading.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The switch remains closed. The slider S is moved along the resistance wire so that the voltmeter reading is $3.1\text{V}$.
On Fig. 7.1, draw a cross $(\times)$ on the resistance wire to show a possible new position of the slider.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The circuit in (b) is altered by changing the battery for one of a different e.m.f. The switch is open.
A student records the following data for the resistance wire:
current in the wire $0.93\text{A}$
mean drift speed of charge carriers $1.3 \times 10^{-3}\text{m s}^{-1}$
number density of charge carriers $9.0 \times 10^{28}\text{m}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Determine the charge $q$ of a charge carrier in the wire suggested by this data.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to the value of $q$, explain why the data recorded by the student cannot be correct.
